source.title: On the different regimes of stochastic gradient descent

record.file_problem: Full paper and supporting information are present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains deep networks with SGD and reports training-loss outcomes, but uses a specific hinge-loss, binary-task setup rather than the claim version’s benchmark recipes.
record.gate_note: The deep-network experiments train until zero training loss; the paper also identifies diverging trainings in phase-diagram figures. It does not test CIFAR-100 or corrupted/random labels. Results it cites from other studies are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study reports zero-loss endpoints for randomly initialized convolutional networks trained with SGD on a binary CIFAR-10 task, bearing on V1 in a new task setting. Its learning-rate experiments do not measure the stability thresholds, curvature dynamics or squared-loss recovery named in V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors derive three SGD regimes for a teacher-student perceptron and find empirical counterparts in deep networks. Critical batch size depends on training-set size and task difficulty; alignment and weight changes can explain performance differences in some settings, while other settings show effects resembling early-stopping regularization.
record.recipe_differences: Uses constant-rate SGD with hinge loss and binary classification tasks, including MobileNet on CIFAR10 and a 5-hidden-layer GELU network on parity MNIST; it does not use the claim versions’ stated benchmark recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate and batch size change the regime; some large learning rates cause divergence. The paper also reports that early stopping changes the CIFAR10 test-error pattern, but does not report it as a training-error comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: The five-hidden-layer GELU network reaches the stated zero-hinge-loss endpoint on parity MNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Randomly initialized fully connected networks can fit parity MNIST with constant-rate SGD in convergent settings.

fits_no_version.finding: SGD exhibits noise-dominated, first-step-dominated and gradient-descent regimes, measured through output alignment, weight changes and test performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch size, learning rate, training-set size and task structure determine distinct SGD regimes and their generalization behavior.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
record.problems: The deep-network training-error outcome is primarily specified as the stopping criterion, rather than separately quantified across conditions. Divergence is marked in figures without condition-level values. Tasks are binary and do not include CIFAR-100 or corrupted/random labels.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted. Figure S6’s individual diverging points are not separately enumerated because the supplied text does not identify their conditions or error values.

untested.parts: Standard ten-class CIFAR-10 classification, CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, Adam, and comparisons of model size, early stopping or regularization on training classification error.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and the effect of adding student neurons.
Training-error comparisons across depths and between plain networks and networks with identity shortcuts.
Comparative initialization effects on training speed, signal propagation and trainable depth.
Initial stability thresholds, transient loss growth followed by recovery, curvature reduction and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization or Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for any listed version. The use of hinge-loss training does not disqualify its observed fitting result. Merely varying learning rates or escaping the lazy regime does not establish V5, and using residual blocks or a particular initialization does not test V3, V4 or V6.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, and comparisons involving smaller models or early stopping are not tested. The CIFAR-10 task is binary animal-versus-rest classification, and the MNIST task is even-versus-odd.

rows.subject: CNN made of several blocks composed of depth-wise, point-wise and standard convolutions plus residual connections (MobileNet)
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD at constant learning rate and batch size on CIFAR10 until training hinge loss and fraction of unfitted training points reached zero.

conditions.value: hinge loss; margin κ = 2−15 in Fig. 1, and κ = 1 in Fig. S6
constant η; varied across phase diagram

rows.measure: Training hinge loss and fraction of training points not fitted
rows.uncertainty: Results averaged over 5 random initialization seeds
rows.locator: Supporting Information 1.B, Eq. 21; Fig. S6 caption
rows.note: The reported protocol defines the endpoint as zero training loss; phase diagrams also mark diverging trainings, without giving their training-error values.
rows.check: Restrict the endpoint to convergent runs: zero loss is the stopping criterion, not evidence that every hyperparameter setting converged. Predictions use F(w,x)=f(w,x)-f(w0,x), so zero hinge loss establishes zero classification error for this centered predictor. Separate the two margins if retaining one condition per row.
